records.issue_text: group.js findMembers reuses the current offset after removeMember, so removing the sole member on the last page leaves offset >= user_count and renders an empty page
records.rationale: In group.js, findMembers clamps offset against the client's stale user_count (`offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`). removeMember calls self.findMembers() immediately after the DELETE, but user_count isn't refreshed before this, so if the removed user was the last one on the final page, the stale offset (>= new total) is sent and the server returns an empty members page with meta.offset echoing the stale value. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff; the edge case is narrow, so moderate confidence.

records.issue_text: group_member.hbs `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves `automatic` against the member User context instead of the group, so the remove link is always shown even for automatic groups
records.rationale: group_member.hbs is rendered per member via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so the template context is the Discourse.User member, not the group. `{{#unless automatic}}` therefore evaluates the User's `automatic` property (undefined/undefined-ish) rather than the group's, so the remove link is always rendered even for automatic groups, where `removeMember` is prohibited (controller returns 422). No controller proxying the group is set up for the view (group-member.js.es6 only sets classNames/templateName), so the mechanism described is correct.

records.issue_text: groups_controller#members takes `limit` directly from params with no cap, allowing `limit=1000000` on large automatic groups to serialize every user and enable resource exhaustion
records.rationale: The diff's new members action sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no maximum and applies it to all groups, whereas the old code only applied a capped-by-caller limit (default 200) to automatic groups; an attacker can now pass limit=1000000 on any visible group and force serialization of every user. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff and is a real security/resource-exhaustion regression.
